title: Day-2 Backup/Restore Toolkit (Private) — Spec Draft (WIP)
body:
Last updated: 2025-02-18 (TB)

Purpose
- Define early requirements + component inventory for Redwood Private backup/restore + DR readiness.
- This is a working doc; we’ll convert stable parts into Confluence runbooks + ADRs.

Audience
- Private Deployments Eng + Control Plane Eng + SRE + Security + Release Eng + Solutions.

Why now (context)
- Enterprise prospects (FinBank, MedData) asking for: deterministic restore, encrypted backups, and a repeatable DR playbook (incl. air-gapped).
- We need something supportable: scripts + hooks + runbooks + validation.

Goals (v0 scope)
1) Consistent backups of Private control-plane state.
2) Deterministic restore into:
   a) an existing cluster (same env) OR
   b) a clean cluster (replacement / DR staging)
3) DR procedures that can meet agreed RPO/RTO targets per archetype.
4) Works in constrained environments:
   - air-gapped on-prem
   - limited outbound egress
   - restricted IAM
5) Ships with:
   - installer CLI commands + optional Helm CronJob
   - reference Terraform patterns (S3 + KMS + IAM)
   - observability (metrics, dashboards, alerts)
   - restore validation tooling + game day plan

Non-goals (explicit)
- Backing up customer application data stored outside Redwood Private.
- A generic “backup all Kubernetes things” solution. We may integrate w/ Velero, but Redwood owns control-plane state backup format and restore sequencing.
- Cross-cloud or cross-architecture migration guarantees in v0 (e.g., AWS->GCP, amd64->arm64). We’ll document what’s supported.
- Restoring GPU model weights caches / data-plane runtime caches (stateless patterns).

Definitions
- Control plane state: minimal set of state required to bring Private environment back to an operational state with correct tenant/config/routing.
- RPO: maximum tolerable data loss window.
- RTO: maximum tolerable time to restore service.
- “Deterministic restore”: given the same inputs (backup artifact + versioned manifests + secrets references), restore converges to the same functional state; drift is either prevented or explicitly reported.

Deployment archetypes (initial)
A) VPC single-region (single cluster)
B) VPC multi-AZ (single region)
C) On-prem connected
D) On-prem air-gapped

Assumptions (confirm)
- Redwood Private installs run on Kubernetes + Helm (installer controls charts and values).
- Control plane has at least one primary datastore (likely Postgres) and uses Kubernetes objects + CRDs for config.
- Secrets are stored in Kubernetes Secrets in many installs today; enterprise customers prefer external secret managers or at minimum KMS at rest.

Component inventory (what exists / likely)
NOTE: inventory is intentionally “loose” until Ethan/Benji confirm canonical list.

Control plane (candidate)
- API / ingress gateway (k8s Service/Ingress/Gateway)
- Authn/authz service + configuration (clients, tokens, keys)
- Config / tenant registry service
- Router policy config (model routing, fallback policies, region/capacity tier rules)
- Model catalog metadata + pinned versions (if persisted)
- Usage/metering service configuration (NOT raw logs)
- Audit log exporter config + retention settings

Stateful datastores (candidate)
- Postgres (primary config DB)
- Redis (cache; should be rehydratable, likely NOT in backup)
- Object storage bucket(s) (customer-managed) for logs/artifacts
- Kubernetes etcd (cluster-level, handled separately via infra runbook)

Kubernetes resources
- Namespaces
- Helm releases + values files
- CRDs (must be present at restore time; ordering matters)
- ConfigMaps/Secrets (policy decision: restore secrets or restore references?)

Backup boundaries (v0)
We are targeting “application-level backup” of Redwood control plane + deterministic redeploy config.

In scope to capture
1) Control plane database snapshot (consistent)
   - includes tenant definitions, routing policies, pinned model versions, config state
   - excludes ephemeral cache tables if possible
2) Installer + Helm configuration required to reapply the deployment
   - chart versions, values (sanitized), image digests
   - cluster-specific settings (domains, region, resource sizing)
3) Kubernetes resources needed for restore sequencing
   - CRDs list + versions
   - Redwood-specific CRs (if present)
4) Secrets handling
   - v0 preference: do NOT include plaintext secret material in the backup artifact
   - include references (Secret names, external secret IDs/ARNs) + checks that required secrets exist pre-restore
   - exception (needs Security sign-off): allow encrypted-in-artifact secrets when external secret manager isn’t available
5) Audit logs
   - separate stream/export (config + evidence), but we need a retention/back-up story; likely “export to customer storage” more than “bundle into same artifact”

Out of scope to capture
- Kubernetes PVs unrelated to Redwood control plane (customer apps, etc.)
- Data-plane pods/state: inference runtime is stateless; restore is redeploy
- “Full cluster recovery” (etcd restore). That’s an infra runbook; we will link it and clarify when to use.

Operator experience (what we’re building)
CLI (private installer)
- rwd-private backup create
  - outputs a backup “bundle” (manifest + encrypted payload)
  - writes to S3/NFS/local path depending on config
- rwd-private backup verify
  - checks checksum + decryptability + manifest consistency
- rwd-private restore apply
  - performs preflight (versions, CRDs present, secrets references available)
  - restores DB + re-applies relevant k8s resources (or ensures Helm values in place)
  - runs post-restore validations + generates a report

Kubernetes automation hooks
- Optional Helm CronJob for scheduled backups
  - retry/backoff
  - resource requests/limits
  - writes metrics
- Optional “restore Job template” used during controlled restore

Terraform patterns (VPC)
- reference module to create:
  - S3 bucket (versioning, lifecycle/retention)
  - KMS key (customer-managed)
  - IAM policies (least privilege) for backup writer + restore reader

Backup artifact format (proposal; aligns w/ ADR-027 direction)
Bundle = directory-like structure (or tar) with:
- manifest.json (human-readable, canonical)
  - backup_id
  - created_at
  - product_version (private installer + chart versions)
  - backup_format_version (semantic-ish; see compatibility section)
  - environment metadata (cluster id/name, region, install mode)
  - included_components list
  - checksums list
  - encryption metadata (kms provider, key id/arn, data key algorithm)
- payload.enc (encrypted tarball)
  - db dump/snapshot (pg_dump or physical snapshot TBD)
  - sanitized helm values + release metadata
  - resource manifests (as needed)
- checksums.txt (sha256)
- signature (on-prem/offline distribution consideration; see below)

Encryption requirements
- Backups MUST be encrypted at rest.
- For cloud (AWS): envelope encryption w/ KMS.
  - backup job gets permission to GenerateDataKey + Encrypt, NOT Decrypt (confirm; restore needs Decrypt).
  - restore job/actor needs Decrypt.
- For on-prem:
  - support “local KMS/HSM provider” via interface OR
  - fallback to operator-provided public key (age/PGP) for artifact encryption.
- Clear policy needed on “what if KMS is down” during scheduled backups.
  - Initial leaning: fail the backup loudly (metrics + alert), do not write plaintext.

Secrets policy (draft)
- Default: do not embed secrets. Backups should capture references and require operator to provide secret material in restore cluster.
- If customer uses Kubernetes Secrets only:
  - option A: treat Secrets as “material” and store them encrypted-in-artifact
  - option B: require customer to re-provision secrets on restore
Open question: what do enterprise customers expect here vs what Security will approve.

Backup consistency strategy
We need “consistent control-plane snapshot” (transactions align with config state).
Options (to be decided with CP Eng):
1) DB-native consistent snapshot (preferred)
   - Postgres: pg_basebackup or snapshot + WAL handling OR pg_dump w/ consistent snapshot
2) App-level quiesce
   - temporarily pause writes (maintenance mode) for brief window
3) Hybrid
   - short quiesce to reduce drift + DB snapshot

Restore sequencing (draft)
0) Preflight
   - confirm target cluster is compatible (k8s version, CRDs, chart versions)
   - confirm backup format version compatibility
   - confirm required secrets references exist (or prompt)
   - confirm access to backup storage backend
1) Bootstrap minimal infra
   - namespaces, service accounts, RBAC
   - CRDs installed (ordering matters)
2) Restore DB
   - ensure DB service reachable
   - restore snapshot/dump
3) Deploy/upgrade control plane
   - Helm install/upgrade with pinned values
   - ensure image digests match expected
4) Apply config layer
   - any CRs/config maps required to reconcile state
5) Post-restore validation
   - health endpoints ready
   - list tenants matches manifest
   - routing policy checksum matches
   - sample request flow (smoke test)
6) Produce a “restore report” artifact
   - what was restored
   - deviations/warnings
   - timestamps (start/end)
   - pointers to logs

Validation / smoke tests (initial set)
- Control plane API ready (liveness + readiness)
- Can authenticate with an admin token (or configured auth method)
- List tenants
- Validate routing policy objects count + checksum
- Ensure “default model route” exists (or customer-defined baseline)
- Optional: run synthetic inference request if data plane is present (may be out-of-scope for pure CP restore)

Observability requirements
Metrics (names TBD; align with Observability Pack)
- backup_last_success_timestamp
- backup_duration_seconds
- backup_bytes_total
- backup_success_total / backup_failure_total
- restore_drill_last_success_timestamp
- restore_drill_duration_seconds
- error categorization labels (auth, storage, kms, validation)

Alerting (draft; SRE review needed)
- Page (prod): no successful backup within 2x backup interval OR consecutive failures > N
- Ticket (non-prod): failures during business hours only
- Restore drill failures: ticket -> page only if repeated + close to release gate

DR drills
- Provide automation to run periodic restore drill in staging.
- Output should be a single report for support/SRE.
- Goal: catch issues like missing CRDs, RBAC permissions, incompatible backup versions.

Compatibility + migrations (v0 intent)
- Backups must be labeled with:
  - product_version
  - backup_format_version
- Restore must hard-fail if the version is known incompatible.
- We need a policy:
  - “N-1 support”: can restore backups from previous minor versions?
  - “same-major only”?
Open question: exact compatibility promise and whether we ship migration tooling.

Storage backends (supported targets)
- S3 (primary for VPC)
  - bucket versioning ON
  - lifecycle policies for retention
  - optional replication (customer choice)
  - SSE-KMS required
- NFS (for on-prem)
  - caution: performance + permission pitfalls
  - require safe mount options + documented defaults
- GCS/Azure: not in v0 unless demand surfaces (track)

Air-gapped packaging requirements
- Backup/restore utilities must be present in offline bundle.
- No external calls required for restore (unless the customer explicitly configures internal endpoints).
- Signed artifacts
  - Release Eng wants a deterministic bundle layout + checksums manifest + signature verification steps.
- Offline docs (HTML/PDF) included.

Security / compliance considerations (notes)
- Audit log retention:
  - likely not bundled in “control plane state” backup
  - must have a documented export/backup process to customer storage
- Evidence:
  - produce restore reports with timestamps and version metadata
  - include checksums + signature verification logs

Customer support boundaries
- We can provide runbooks + “expected restore report”, but support should not require deep cluster surgery.
- If restore requires etcd recovery, we route to infra runbook + appropriate escalation.

Open questions (tracked)
1) Canonical inventory: exact list of CP stateful components (DBs, CRDs, config objects).
2) DB snapshot method: pg_dump vs physical snapshot + WAL.
3) Quiesce: do we require a maintenance window? How long? What endpoints/control-plane mode needed?
4) Secrets: allow encrypted secrets in artifact by default or only as opt-in? What are acceptable exceptions?
5) KMS downtime: fail closed vs degrade to local encryption? (Security strongly prefers fail closed.)
6) Multi-cluster DR: do we support “restore into new cluster and flip DNS” as first-class?
7) Cross-region restore in VPC: do we recommend bucket replication? Do we ship docs only?
8) How much k8s state do we capture vs rely on Helm reproducibility?
   - debate: backup CRDs/resources vs pin chart + values and re-install.
9) Restore validation depth: do we require a sample inference request to claim success?
10) Retention defaults: what’s our recommended schedule + retention for each archetype?

Risks / known failure modes (early)
- Missing CRDs / wrong ordering -> restore breaks (seen in customer-like envs)
- RBAC too tight for CronJob -> backups silently fail unless we alert
- Slow object storage/NFS -> job times out; need chunking + timeouts + retries
- Clock skew -> signatures/checks fail; need to document time sync requirement
- Large DB -> backup duration exceeds customer RTO expectations; need sizing guidance

Proposed milestones (rough)
- Phase 0: requirements capture + RPO/RTO matrix + threat model
- Phase 1: backup create + verify, ADR for format/encryption, first draft runbooks
- Phase 2: restore apply + validation report + helm/terraform hooks + dashboards
- Phase 3: game day + hardening + support enablement + release checklist

Notes / TODOs (owner)
- [TB] Schedule review with Security (Marcus/Hanae): secrets policy + encryption specifics.
- [Ethan] Confirm CP component list + which tables/objects represent tenant/routing/policy state.
- [Neha/Sean] Define SLOs + paging thresholds and how to avoid false positives during maintenance.
- [Connor] Confirm offline signing approach and where verification should happen (CI gate vs runtime).
- [Markus/Fatima] Gather customer constraints on permitted storage backends and acceptable restore workflows.

Appendix: strawman CLI
- Backup:
  rwd-private backup create \
    --namespace redwood-private \
    --backend s3 \
    --bucket <bucket> \
    --prefix backups/<cluster-id>/ \
    --kms-key-arn <arn> \
    --include helm-values,control-plane-db \
    --output-manifest ./backup-manifest.json

- Restore:
  rwd-private restore apply \
    --from s3://<bucket>/backups/<cluster-id>/<backup-id>/ \
    --target-namespace redwood-private \
    --preflight-only=false \
    --validate=true \
    --report-out ./restore-report.json
